::: {.why}
The spread you measured last night is probably as large as the gap between your best and worst model family, which means most published comparisons at this signal level are reporting seed noise.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the across-seed standard deviation of out-of-sample performance and compare it against the across-model differences.
- State the reporting rule you will follow for the rest of the phase.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Quantify it across the board: for every model family, refit with ten seeds and report the mean and standard deviation of out-of-sample R-squared. Then plot the across-model differences against the across-seed spreads. Any comparison smaller than the spread is not a comparison.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Adopt the fix, which is cheap: every reported model result from here is the average of an ensemble across seeds, with the across-seed spread reported alongside. Ensembling also improves the result, so this costs nothing except computation.
:::
:::

::: {.deliverable}
Across-seed spreads for every model family plotted against the across-model differences, and the ensembling rule adopted.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your boosting model beats ridge by 0.0004 in R-squared and your seed spread is 0.0006. What do you report?
:::
